question: A ______ is a disturbance that moves through a medium when the particles of the medium set neighbouring particles into motion.
solution:
The correct answer is __**wave**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **wave** is a **disturbance** that travels through a **medium**, transferring **energy** from one location to another without the permanent transfer of **mass**.
 
• When a wave moves through a medium, the **particles** of that medium do not travel along with the wave; instead, they **oscillate** or vibrate about their **fixed mean positions**.
 
• The process occurs when a vibrating particle sets its **neighboring particles** into **motion** through **intermolecular forces** or collisions, thereby propagating the disturbance further.
 
• This **energy transport** mechanism is fundamental to all types of **mechanical waves**, such as **sound waves** in air or **seismic waves** in the Earth's crust.
 
• The **medium** can be a **solid**, **liquid**, or **gas**, and its physical properties like **density** and **elasticity** determine the speed at which the wave travels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Waves:**

 
 
• **Longitudinal Waves**: In these waves, the particles of the medium vibrate **parallel** to the direction of wave propagation. A common example is **sound waves**, which consist of **compressions** (high pressure) and **rarefactions** (low pressure).
 
• **Transverse Waves**: In these waves, the particles vibrate **perpendicular** to the direction of wave movement. Examples include **water waves** and **light waves**.
 
 
 
• **Wave Parameters:**
 
 
• **Frequency**: This refers to the **number of oscillations** or cycles per unit of **time**. It is measured in **Hertz (Hz)**. While frequency is a characteristic of a wave, it is not the disturbance itself.
 
• **Wavelength**: The distance between two consecutive points in the same phase, such as from **crest to crest** or **trough to trough**.
 
• **Amplitude**: The **maximum displacement** of the particles of the medium from their **original undisturbed position**. It represents the **energy** or **intensity** of the wave.
 
 
 
• **Wave Speed**: The speed (**v**) of a wave is calculated by the product of its **frequency (f)** and **wavelength**. The formula is expressed as **v = f × wavelength**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Phase**: It describes the **position** and **direction** of motion of a particle at a specific **instant of time** within a cycle. Points in the same phase are at the same stage of their vibration.
 
• **Tone**: In the context of sound, a **tone** is a sound of a **distinct pitch** and **quality**, often resulting from a **single frequency** or a combination of **harmonics**.
 
• **Mechanical vs. Electromagnetic Waves**: Unlike **mechanical waves** (like sound), **electromagnetic waves** (like radio waves or X-rays) do not require a **material medium** and can propagate through a **vacuum** at the **speed of light** (approx **3 × 10⁸ m/s**).
 
• **Acoustics**: The branch of **physics** that deals with the study of mechanical waves in gases, liquids, and solids including **vibration, sound, ultrasound, and infrasound**.
